issue.title: sase revive-log --since crashes: _resolve_since strips tzinfo but event timestamps are tz-aware
issue.description:
`sase revive-log --since <range>` always crashes with a naive-vs-aware datetime comparison.

Root cause (read in source on master d62a459a2):
- `src/sase/logs/run_log.py::_parse_event_timestamp` was changed to return tz-aware datetimes in the configured timezone (its docstring says since/until bounds come from `parse_daterange` as aware configured-tz datetimes).
- `src/sase/logs/revive_log_cli.py::_resolve_since` still does `start.replace(tzinfo=None)`, so it passes a naive `since` into `iter_revive_events`, and `ts < since` raises.

Fix: stop stripping tzinfo in `_resolve_since` (keep the aware bound), and add a CLI-level regression test for `--since`.

Found while auditing the 2026-09-25 core schema-skew outage: revive history could not be queried for the post-mortem.

task_type_fields.impact: Every --since query of the revive audit log fails, so revive/retry history is unavailable for incident post-mortems.
task_type_fields.repro: Run `sase revive-log --since -1d` -> TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes at run_log.py iter_revive_events (`ts < since`).

payload.description: Sibling timezone-mismatch defect (configured-tz vs host/naive datetimes); fixes touch similar datetime conventions
